producer_report.summary: The drain now holds a line of work once it has two attempts that did not land. It stops retrying that line and passes its items over as "awaiting diagnosis", which is not counted as a failure. A line is the scope guard's grouping (`group_lines`). An attempt counts as not landed if its job was rejected or failed (environment stops are not counted, as for signal T1). It also counts if the job closed landed locally but the host did not take it. The host took a job when its pull-request link `state` is `Landed` (new `PrLink::taken_by_host()`) or a landing record names it. Either one removes the job from the unlanded count. A job with no link at all is treated as landed, so it is retried as before. `request_records` is now a wrapper over `request_records_with`, and only the hold passes the "unlanded" predicate, so signals T1 to T5 and pauses are unchanged. `Athena::line_holds` derives the hold from the records and link files each time and writes nothing, so it lifts when a link turns Landed or the request words change. `Steps::held` has a default of "nothing held", so other implementations of `Steps` compile unchanged. In `Drain::attempts` the hold is checked at the top of the `passed.is_none()` block and again after the item's last failed attempt, in the order paused, flagged, held. It is never checked between a passed job and its landing, so an item's own landing retry still runs. `Drain::prepare` also holds those items like paused ones, and `drain --help` mentions the hold. The diagnosis job, its role brief and schema, a line field on every job, and the `athena status` display are not built here. The CHANGELOG says so. Tests: five scope-guard tests (rig_counting) and six tests in a new `line_hold` module in `tests/drain.rs` on the real `drain::drain` and `drain::plan`. I confirmed the drain tests are not vacuous: with `HOLD_ATTEMPTS` temporarily set to 1, four of the six `line_hold` tests failed. The full `cargo test --locked` passed once, before the last small refactor; I then re-ran the `scope_guard`, whole `drain`, `policy` and `mirrors` tests, `cargo fmt --check` and clippy after it.

open_issues: A pull request waiting on checks has an Open link and no landing record, so it counts as not landed until it is seen merged. One rejection plus one merging job can hold a line. This is the documented fallback, stated in the CHANGELOG, and the hold lifts when the link turns Landed.

The hold applies only to the drain; `athena go` and `athena retry` do not check it, as the plan intended. A held line therefore has no release command; it lifts when a link turns Landed or the request words change.
Under max_concurrency > 1, two items of one line can start before either fails, so the hold can overrun by one attempt (the scope-guard pause has the same race).
I did not run the replay of accepted readings myself; no reading rule was changed.
mistakes: I first put the per-pull-request wording in pr.rs (`LinkState::words`) and let scope_guard's `hold_note` do the formatting, so drain.rs never read `LinkState`. The plan and criterion 5 wanted drain.rs to match on `LinkState`. I moved the wording into `RealSteps::held` and removed `words`.

I started the full `cargo test --locked` before that last refactor, so the single full run does not cover the final edits. I covered them with targeted re-runs of the scope_guard, drain, policy and mirrors tests, clippy and fmt.
learnings: `go` records a local Landed outcome before the drain lands the pull request, so a collision job reads as Accepted in the records. Only the pull-request link's `state` field says whether the host took it.

The fake agent's Scenario adds a unique CHANGELOG line per distinct edit set, so a second job that repeats the same README edit has no diff and does not land. The `numbered` test helper replaces both the README text and the CHANGELOG line per call so each job has a real diff.
Drain::pass_over prints one 'plan <id> passed over: <reason>' line per item per run, so tests can read the end of each item from the Ui lines.
The build slot is exclusive (`no build slot free for 300 s`, exit 75): a background `cargo test` blocks every other cargo build until it finishes.
Producer-role shell hooks block head, tail, grep, wc, sed and echo, so redirects and pipes cannot be used; use `cargo test -q` and the dedicated tools.
desires: A way to wait on a background build without polling: the build slot was held by my own background test run for about 15 minutes and blocked clippy.
A readable path for the background task output file, so I could see test progress.
